supporting_observations.claim: The domain controller recorded creation of the alerted account svc_update at 13:44:34 UTC, with ken.ito as the subject.

About one second later, ken.ito added svc_update to the domain Administrators group. This is inconsistent with the stated help-desk practice that temporary accounts are Seasonal-only and never administrators.

Just before the account events, WS-EBROOKS-01 logged a Type 10 remote interactive session for ken.ito from 203.0.113.133. The inventory says remote administration is only from WS-KITO-01 and there is no VPN; this is a significant contextual mismatch, though the available records do not tie that session directly to the account-creation logon.

Two seconds after the account creation, WS-EBROOKS-01 recorded ken.ito creating a hidden PowerShell scheduled task whose encoded arguments contain a web request to 203.0.113.133/a.ps1. This is suspicious activity on the same host and near the alerted account activity, but the task record uses a different logon ID from the account-creation record.

known_telemetry_limitations: The account creation record's SubjectLogonId is 0xbff67aa, while the recorded ken.ito remote session on WS-EBROOKS-01 has LogonId 0xf04b2c1; the provided evidence does not establish how those sessions relate.
The supplied records do not show the process or command that created svc_update, or the authentication/session details corresponding to the account event's SubjectLogonId.
The records establish account creation and administrator-group addition, but do not show whether the account was subsequently used or what access it exercised.
claims_not_established: That the person ken.ito personally performed the account creation or administrator-group change; the logs identify the account as the subject but do not establish who controlled the session.
That the remote session from 203.0.113.133 caused the account creation or scheduled-task creation.
That svc_update was created as part of the scheduled svc-inventory password rotation; the calendar names svc-inventory, not svc_update, and the supplied records do not document the rotation workflow.
Whether the account or scheduled task was used successfully after creation.
additional_evidence_needed: Correlate DC-BLU-01 logon and privileged-account audit records for ken.ito, including the session associated with SubjectLogonId 0xbff67aa.
Collect process, PowerShell, and command-line telemetry on DC-BLU-01 and WS-EBROOKS-01 around 13:40–13:45 UTC to identify the account-creation and group-change mechanism.
Verify the provenance and ownership of the 203.0.113.133 connection and scheduled-task payload, and determine whether the task executed.
Check change approvals and the svc-inventory rotation/update records to confirm whether any approved activity accounts for svc_update.
unrelated_findings: Dropbox was launched and accessed from WS-EBROOKS-01, although Dropbox is not among the listed approved services; this is separate from the account-management alert. Records: T187-00060, T187-00064, T187-00065.

WS-EBROOKS-01 accessed a Google Docs document, while the inventory lists Microsoft 365 / OneDrive as approved cloud services; investigate separately if policy requires. Records: T187-00320, T187-00321.

Cisco AnyConnect's vpnagent.exe ran on WS-EBROOKS-01 despite the stated no-VPN environment; this observation alone does not establish a VPN connection and is separate from the alerted account activity. Records: T187-00251, T187-00252.
